Each hour: time, direction and speed (knots, g = gust), odds of 12kt or more, regime, waves, tide height in ft with r rising or f falling. OUTFLOW NOT RIDDEN = Squamish outflow, never recommend. OFF DIR = direction does not work at that spot.
Riding light (first light to last light, Vancouver): Fri, Oct 30 7:23am to 6:28pm; Sat, Oct 31 7:25am to 6:26pm; Sun, Nov 1 6:26am to 5:25pm. Hours outside that are dark and not listed; never suggest riding then.

Guillermo's own take for Fri, Oct 30 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): Outflow morning, and it’s stronger than the page. Pam Rocks read N 30 at 6am, and Pemberton is 5.9 hPa above it and still building. On mornings like this, about 9 in 10 of the next 3 hours stayed 20kt+. EC has a strong wind warning for Howe Sound: northerly 30, easing to 10 to 15 near noon.

My pick is Porteau from first light (7:23am) to about 10:30am, NNE 22 to 28 gusting 30, with 3 to 4ft of swell. Go early: the tide floods all morning to a 15.8ft high at 10:41am, which may flatten the swell as it fills. If Pam Rocks drops under 22 it’s done, and it should die by 11am either way.

Everywhere else is light. The English Bay buoy has N 12 to 18 and Sand Heads N 10 to 19, but that’s offshore for Jericho and Boundary Bay, and Point Atkinson is only NNW 3 to 6. Squamish is an outflow, so boat only.

Saturday looks like another outflow: EC calls northerly 15 to 25.

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 04:00 PM PCT 30 October 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Tonight and Saturday. Strong wind warning in effect. Wind northerly outflow 10 to 20 knots increasing to northerly outflow 20 to 30 Saturday evening.

EC marine forecast, Strait of Georgia (south of Nanaimo) (issued 04:00 PM PCT 30 October 2026): Tonight and Saturday. Wind light becoming east 5 to 15 knots early this evening then becoming light late Saturday morning. Wind becoming northwest 10 to 15 Saturday evening.

Track record, last 30 days: Porteau Cove (scored at Pam Rocks): typical miss 3.3kt, caught 68% of windy hours, 16% false alarms; Steveston - Garry Point Park (scored at Sand Heads): typical miss 2.58kt, caught 80% of windy hours, 18% false alarms; Tsawwassen Ferry Terminal Causeway (scored at Tsawwassen Ferry Terminal): typical miss 2.79kt, caught 57% of windy hours, 20% false alarms; Erwin Park (scored at Point Atkinson): typical miss 2.86kt, caught 34% of windy hours, 32% false alarms. Other spots are not measured yet.
